cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, just heard from the LORD how his brother Aaron goes into the Most Holy Place to make atonement for Israel's sins (Leviticus 16:2, 17, 34). Now the LORD has a new message for Aaron, Aaron's sons and all the Israelites. That's the WHOLE group chat, friend, so nobody gets to say they missed the message.

cards.question: Say someone from the house of Israel slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat, in the camp or outside it. God says he must bring it somewhere instead, to present it as an offering to the LORD. Where?

answers.text: The entrance to the Tent of Meeting
The banks of the Jordan River

cards.question: God says a man who slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat without bringing it to the Tent of Meeting shall incur ___ and must be cut off from among his people.
God says the Israelites will now bring the LORD the sacrifices they've been offering somewhere else. Where have they been offering them?

cards.text: Now those sacrifices come to the priest at the entrance, as peace offerings. The priest splatters the blood on the LORD's altar and burns the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Then God names something the Israelites have been doing with their sacrifices that has to stop. He calls this a permanent statute for the generations to come.

cards.question: What does God say the Israelites must no longer do with their sacrifices?
God says anyone who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice but doesn't bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting must be cut off from his people, even a foreigner living among the Israelites.

cards.text: Now God turns to blood: if anyone eats any blood, Israelite or foreigner, God says, "I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people." Friend, I got slid into a junk drawer and cut off from my whole family once, and I would NOT recommend it.

cards.question: Then God explains why eating blood is off-limits. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The life of the flesh is in the blood
The sickness of the flesh is in the blood
The curse of the ground is in the blood

cards.question: God says He has given the blood to the Israelites to make atonement for their souls. Where?

cards.text: God says it AGAIN: no Israelite and no foreigner living among them may eat blood.

cards.question: An Israelite or a foreigner living among them hunts down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten. What does God say he must do with its blood?

answers.text: Drain it and cover it with dirt
Pour it out on the altar

cards.text: Then God says it once more: the life of all flesh is its blood, so no one may eat the blood of any living thing. When somebody keeps saying the same thing, friend, that's the part you write on your hand.
Then a different case: someone, native or foreigner, eats something found dead or mauled by wild beasts.

cards.question: Someone eats an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts. What does God say that person must do?

answers.text: Wash his clothes and bathe with water
Offer a lamb at the altar
Stay outside the camp for a week

cards.question: God says the person who ate an animal found dead stays unclean for seven days after washing.

cards.text: Laundry day AND bath night, back to back, friend. And if he skips it, God says "he shall bear his iniquity."
That's the end of this message, friend. But trust me, the LORD's not done talking to Moses, so keep that apron on.
